name: DockRoute
description: DockRoute watches your running containers, reads their dockroute.* labels and reconciles the matching DNS records (and Cloudflare Tunnel routes) in a pluggable provider. Your Docker labels are the source of truth; DockRoute makes the provider match them, and it never alters or deletes a record it cannot prove it manages, because every record it creates is paired with an ownership TXT record in the ExternalDNS style. It has no web interface: it is a background reconciler, check the container logs to see what it is doing.
short_desc: External-DNS for plain Docker hosts, driven by container labels
author: Danilo Dorgam

form_fields.label: DNS provider: "log" is a zero-credential dry run that only prints the desired state; switch to "cloudflare" when you are ready.
Ownership id written to the companion TXT records. Lets several DockRoute instances share a zone safely.
sync = create, update and delete owned records; upsert-only = never delete; create-only = never update or delete.
Seconds a record must stay gone before DockRoute deletes it. Protects against container restarts; 0 deletes immediately.
Fallback record value (IP or CNAME target) for containers that omit the dockroute.target label. Usually this server's LAN or WAN IP.
Optional comma-separated allowlist of DNS zones DockRoute may touch. Empty = every zone the token can see.
Interval of the periodic full reconcile that backs up the Docker event stream.
Required when the provider is cloudflare. Needs Zone -> DNS -> Edit, plus Account -> Cloudflare Tunnel -> Edit for tunnel publishing.
Only needed for Cloudflare Tunnel publishing.
Only needed for Cloudflare Tunnel publishing. Uses an existing tunnel, so you keep running cloudflared yourself.
